- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 2% from prior high), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +1.5% above peak or use 3-day moving average.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.4) within 3–5 days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply 0.8–1.2% upward bias for first 7 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.3+), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and smooth transitions using 5-day weighted average.
- If recent sentiment is flat (±0.1) and price is trending sideways, model overfits to recent noise; use 3-day simple moving average for smoothing.
